title: Making Intelligence: Ethical Values in IQ and ML Benchmarks

bias_targets.methodology: Conceptual analysis and historical comparison examining how structural inequities and discriminatory practices in human intelligence (IQ) testing parallel potential ethical risks in ML benchmark design.
Conceptual analysis of how ML evaluation benchmarks and ground-truth datasets can reify rigid social constructs, specifically by entrenching normative visual categories of gender.

Philosophical evaluation of external validity choices in ML benchmarks, questioning the ability of datasets to account for cross-cultural differences (e.g., in toxicity detection) without defaulting to dominant cultural norms.
Conceptual critique highlighting how the choice of external phenomena in benchmarks often systematically favors specific languages, such as American English, over others.
Historical and philosophical analysis of the ableist consequences of standardized cognitive testing and how narrow definitions of intelligence can marginalize neurodiverse populations.
